_comment: issue #2962: classification of every hooks.json command registration. class is one of invariant-injecting|observability. invariant-injecting = the hook's absence leaves the session running without a rule it establishes or enforces (directive text, role state, gate deny logic, obligation tracking). observability = the hook only reports/warns/records; its absence loses signal, not a rule. wrapped=false marks the one registration (pretooluse-dispatcher.sh) that is deliberately fail-closed and bypasses fail-open-wrapper.sh entirely -- its class is recorded for completeness but the visible-fail-open notice mechanism (fail-open-wrapper.sh) never applies to it, and this file does not change its fail-closed posture. Read together with test_hook_classification.py, which checks this file against hooks.json mechanically rather than trusting this comment.

registrations.rationale: refreshes the installed checkout; the script's own header calls offline failure fine -- nothing downstream depends on this having run

pre-existing gap found while adding this issue's own SessionStart entry (issue #3129, commit 638620e4, never got one): the automatic caller of amends_index.py's backlink-write landing step -- absence leaves a merged amends: edge unlinked, same non-enforcing shape as self-update.sh (records a cross-reference, no gate deny logic depends on it having run)

issue #3231: pulls the skill-repository managed-clone fetch forward to session start with a printed notice so --skills doesn't hit an empty corpus on first spawn; absence just defers the same fetch to that first spawn, same as before this issue

issue #3231: prints a git-identity / docs/specs/approvers.md remedy early instead of letting the failure surface deep in a spawned session's git commit or require_board() exit -- read-only, no gate deny logic depends on this having run

snapshots session-role provenance that approval-gate.sh and other gates trust instead of a later, model-influenced env read (issue #698) -- absence leaves those gates unable to enforce the role invariant
injects this system's always-on invariants every turn (issue #2962's own canonical example)

dispatches all 20 PreToolUse deny gates; deliberately fail-closed (command -v python3 || exit 2) and MUST stay outside fail-open-wrapper.sh -- classified here for completeness, not to route it through the visible-fail-open notice
turn-budget warning only; the real --max-turns enforcement lives in the CLI outside this repo

issue #3073: reads its own state file and, for a still-open violation, emits advisory additionalContext naming the commit and the missing row -- it cannot deny or revert a commit that already landed (PreToolUse fires on the NEXT tool call, after the fact), so this is a nudge, not a rule. The strong deny-before-write guarantee for this class of omission still lives entirely in gate-registration-guard.sh's own PreToolUse/`--cached` check, unchanged by this pair. Not copied from post-landing-obligation-gate.sh despite the superficial 'reads/writes a state file' resemblance: nothing outside this hook's own pre-mode ever reads OTR_GRG_POST_STATE_DIR, so there is no downstream enforcement decision this file's presence or absence changes -- unlike post-landing-obligation-gate.sh's record, which the northpole loop actually consults.
post-mode only bumps a per-session denial-signature counter; no rule enforced or injected at this registration
opens the post-landing verification obligation record the northpole loop depends on (issue #1098) -- absence means a landed fix silently owes no tracked verification

issue #3073: greps a just-run `git commit`'s own success line out of tool_response and, on a miss, writes a pending-violation record for its pre-mode sibling to later report -- the script's own header states plainly this mode is 'pure side-effect, always exit 0' and 'cannot deny'. Same reasoning as its pre-mode sibling: no other gate reads the state file it writes, so nothing downstream is silently weakened by this registration's absence -- only the follow-up nudge is lost, which is signal, not a rule.
same warning-only class as its pre-mode sibling
shortens the fail -> re-edit rework loop by surfacing lint/test signal early; absence only slows feedback, no rule is lost
best-effort turn-END watchdog re-arm; the script's own header says do not overclaim -- it widens an existing mechanism, it does not establish one
structurally enforces the approval-reply shape (issue #411); already self-fail-closed via its own trap, but a wrapper-level crash before that trap resolves still means the invariant went unchecked
the merged per-skill verdict obligation gate (issue #2039/#2138) -- absence means a session's skill-verdict obligation goes unchecked and unreported

issue #3229: live wiring for issue #3061's standing-delegation manifest -- on a covered, clean episode it refuses the stop outright (decision:"block"); absence means a covered ask reaches the operator that a recorded delegation already answered, the exact gap PR #3220's tenth verification named

surfaces an orchestrator's issue-body amendment into a running worker session's context via additionalContext (issue #3129); absence loses the mid-flight correction signal but enforces no rule and blocks nothing
